title: High-Dimensionality Flow Cytometry for Immune Function Analysis of Dissected Implant Tissues
protocol: Add 5 mL of HEPES buffer into 500 mL of RPMI medium and shake well.
Store the prepared medium at 4°C until further use.
Prepare a 1:1000 viability dye solution by adding 1 μL of the viability dye to 999 μL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and vortex the solution.
Store the viability dye solution in the dark at 4 °C until further use.
Prepare the staining buffer by adding 1 g of bovine serum albumin (BSA) to 100 mL of PBS, and vortex the solution until BSA is completely dissolved.
Store the staining buffer at 4 °C until further use.
Set up a 6-well plate with 70 μm cell strainers in each well.
Add 3 ml of prepared medium into each well, and incubate on ice.
Store the remaining media (2 ml/well) in an incubator or water bath at 37 °C for suspending the calculated amount of collagenase and DNase I.
Place dissected implants/tissue into plates, and dice finely using scissors.
Alternatively, utilize a mechanical disruption method using a tissue dissociator or hand-held homogenizer.
Dissect out the spleen to utilize as a staining control in each run.
Add collagenase and DNase I to the remaining RPMI that has been warmed to 37 °C.
Add 2 mL of the complete enzyme solution to each well.
Place the plates in an incubated shaker for 45 min at 37 °C and 100 rpm.
Chop 3-4 mm from the end of a 1000 μL tip with scissors to prepare a suspension-dispensing tip.
Pipette the suspension in the wells up and down to mix it thoroughly using the chopped tip after incubation.
Place the cell strainer on top of a 50 mL conical tube.
Pass the digested solution through the cell strainer.
Rinse the wells with 1x PBS solution.
Transfer the rinse volume through the strainer.
Add washes of the strainer with 1x PBS solution until the volume in the tube reaches 50 mL.
Maintain the 1x PBS at room temperature.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1000 µL of 1x PBS and transfer to a microcentrifuge tube.
Mix 10 µL of cell suspension with 10 µL of trypan blue.
Load the suspension on counting chamber slides for automatic cell counter or hemocytometer under microscope.
Alternatively, use flow cytometry cell counting beads.
Estimate the total number of cells.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension required for staining 1 × 10^6 cells per sample and 0.5 × 10^6 cells for each compensation and FMO control.
Dispense the calculated volume of cell suspension into V-bottom 96-well plate wells.
Make up to 100 µL with 1x PBS.
Centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in the sample wells and in a compensation control well with 100 µL of a 1:1000 solution of the viability dye.
Resuspend cells in other compensation, FMO, and unstained wells with 100 µL of 1x PBS.
Incubate the cells in the dark for 30 min at 4 °C.
Prepare a surface antibody cocktail for staining the sample and FMO controls: 50 µL per sample or FMO.
After incubation, add 100 µl of 1x PBS to each well.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in the compensation, FMO, and unstained wells with 50 µL of 1x PBS.
Add 50 µL of the antibody cocktail to the respective sample wells and FMO wells.
Add the respective antibodies to the different compensation wells.
Incubate the plate for 45 min in the dark at 4 °C.
After incubation, add 150 µL of staining buffer in each well.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells with 200 µL of staining buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend samples in 200 µL of staining buffer if analyzing without fixation.
Proceed to section 6 on cytometer setup and sample analysis after resuspension.
Aspirate the supernatant after washing if fixing the cells.
Add 100 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde as fixative for cell samples.
Proceed to section 5 on intracellular staining if required.
Incubate cells in the dark at 4 °C for 20 min.
Add 100 µL of 1x PBS after incubation.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend in 1x PBS.
Centrifuge cells again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the cells in 200 µL of staining buffer after final centrifugation.
Store samples at 4 °C prior to flow cytometric analysis.
Add 100 µL of appropriate buffer for intracellular markers after fixation and permeabilization.
Centrifuge cells at 350 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant, then resuspend pellets in fixative-permeabilizing agent solution.
Centrifuge cells again at 350 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend pellets with intracellular antibodies diluted in appropriate buffer.
Incubate the cell suspension in the dark for 45 min at 4 °C.
Add 150 µL of the appropriate buffer, and centrifuge the suspension at 350 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant, and re-suspend the cells in 200 µL of staining buffer followed by centrifugation at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate and re-suspend the cells in 200 µL of staining buffer for flow cytometric analysis.
Prepare compensation beads immediately before running the samples if utilizing bead-based compensation as opposed to cell-based compensation.

Label separate microcentrifuge tubes for each fluorochrome-conjugated antibody, and add 100 µL of 1x PBS followed by one full drop of anti-mouse negative control compensation beads and one drop of positive control compensation beads to each tube.
Add 1 µL of the appropriate antibody to each separate tube.
Vortex and incubate for 5 min before acquisition.
Calibrate the flow cytometer before each experiment by running the cytometer setup with the tracking beads.
Adjust the flow cytometer using an unstained sample on a side scatter (SSC) versus forward scatter (FSC) plot.
Ensure the cell population is centered and not off-scale.
Run the stained sample briefly to adjust voltages for FSC and SSC.
Verify that no events fall outside the logarithmic scale of each channel.
Record 5,000 events for each compensation control.
Gate positive and negative populations based on staining.
Calculate the compensation matrix.
Run samples and gather at least 1,000 events for populations of interest.
